modelType: Logistic regression, L2 penalty, scikit-learn 1.9.1 (lbfgs, max_iter 2000, random_state 20261107)
intendedUse: Educational early warning on this ledger: rank days of the same account by deficit risk so a report reader or a game mechanic can point at the conditions that precede an overdraft. Every feature row uses only information available the night before the day it scores, so a score for day t is issued before day t happens. It is a demonstration artifact for the Sheridan Datathon 2026 entry, not a deployed underwriting tool.
notIntendedUse: Credit, lending, or any decision about a real person or account.
Scoring customers of a bank or insurance product.
Transferring the coefficients to a different account, year, or income cadence without refitting and revalidating.

data.syntheticNotice: The ledger is SYNTHETIC: seed 20261107, generator scripts/generate_mock_ledger.py, no real bank data. The model and its recipe transfer unchanged to the real Tangerine dataset; only the input CSV changes.
data.target: same day deficit: closing balance below 0 CAD on that calendar day (86 events in the ledger)
data.alternativeTargetConsidered: next day closing balance below 1,000 CAD; fit as robustness on the same night before feature rows, so that check reads as a two day ahead screen (test AUC reported in metrics.robustnessAlternativeTestAuc). The same day negative label was chosen because it is threshold free and the data supports it with 86 events.

features.indicators: day of week (7 levels, Monday reference) and month (12 levels, November reference)
features.nightBeforeRule: every feature row uses only information available the night before day t: trailing windows end at t minus 1, days since payroll is measured through t minus 1, and the day of week and month indicators are calendar facts known in advance; day t itself never enters its own feature row (the first ledger day has no prior night and is not modeled)
features.excludedByDesign: current closing balance; excluding it keeps the model a forward looking screen instead of an identity

split.splitRule: latest month start that leaves at least 30 deficit events in the test segment (enforced in code, so the documented date cannot drift from the data)
split.hyperparameterSelection: TimeSeriesSplit on the training window only, scoring roc_auc

metrics.targetDefinition: same day deficit: closing balance below 0 CAD on that calendar day (86 events in the ledger)
metrics.decisionRule: predicted deficit when probability is at or above 0.5
metrics.robustnessAlternativeTarget: next day closing balance below 1,000 CAD (threshold variant)

limitations: One synthetic account and one year of daily rows (364 samples, 86 events): uncertainty around the test AUC is wide and no confidence interval is claimed.

Strong concept drift: the account balance rises monotonically after the deficit season, so test months are out of distribution for the training months (train AUC versus test AUC in metrics shows the gap).
The current closing balance is excluded by design, which keeps the model honest as a forward screen but caps discrimination; an autoregressive balance feature would score much higher and say less.

Raw accuracy at the 0.5 threshold sits below the majority class baseline because the class balance shifts sharply between train and test; AUC is the headline metric and the confusion matrix is reported in full.
Correlation, not causation: coefficients describe association inside this ledger. days_since_payday raising the odds does not mean waiting longer causes a deficit.
Month indicators memorize this ledger's calendar (the November to April deficit season) and carry no meaning for another year.
fairnessCaveats: The dataset has a single synthetic persona and no demographic fields; results cannot be attributed to any protected group and must not be used to group or rank real people.
Because the persona is synthetic, any fairness assessment here is a method statement only: applying this recipe to real bank data would require subgroup calibration and a fairness review before use.

The strong train versus test base rate shift (53 percent versus 14 percent deficit days) means a fixed 0.5 threshold would over warn in the early period and under warn later; deployment would need recalibration, which is out of scope for this entry.
Deficit labels reflect one account's trajectory; income shocks, employment changes, and emergency expenses are not modeled, so a low score is not evidence of financial wellbeing.
correlationNotCausation: These coefficients are associations observed in one synthetic ledger. They do not establish that changing a feature would change the deficit risk, and they must not be presented as causal effects or used to make decisions about real people.
